message.content:
Audit and fix the Nxeon CUSTOMER PORTAL in LIGHT MODE. The portal was designed in dark mode and light mode was added quickly, so many things look wrong in light: unreadable or low-contrast text, dark-only colours hard-coded (bg-slate-900, text-white, white/[0.03] borders, etc.), invisible borders/dividers, glows meant for dark, logos/icons/images that vanish on white, broken charts, inputs/selects/date pickers, modals/drawers/toasts/tooltips/dropdowns, code blocks, badges, skeleton loaders, scrollbars, and the 3rd-party embeds (Stripe card form, xterm console, noVNC, file manager, editors).

SCOPE: literally every customer-facing page under app/dashboard/** and every sub-page/tab/state, including the full deploy wizard (every product: VPS, every game family, hosting, email, domains, SSL; every step), server pages and all their tabs (overview, console, files, mods, settings, backups, network, billing...), billing/invoices/wallet/checkout, support (tickets, live chat, help), domains/DNS, SSL, mail, settings/security/2FA, refer/partner, What's New dialog + changelog, offers, notifications, onboarding, empty/loading/error states, modals and confirm dialogs, and mobile 390px as well as desktop 1440. Find how the theme is toggled (the light/dark switch + its storage/cookie/class) and how tokens are defined (tailwind config, globals.css, CSS variables) before anything else. Admin pages are OUT of scope. Private-preview pages (/dashboard/mod-builder, /dashboard/dedicated) are in scope too.

METHOD
1. Inventory every route file under app/dashboard (list it in your report) plus the client components that render tabs/modals/states.
2. Run the app against a THROWAWAY database, never prod: look at how earlier agents did authenticated Playwright screenshots with seeded data (e.g. /root/agent-notes/mods-rework, /root/agent-notes/support-overhaul, /root/agent-notes/modbuilder-preview/seed.ts + shot.mjs, /root/agent-notes/dedicated-preview). Seed realistic data so states render (servers of several kinds incl. game servers, invoices, tickets, domains, etc.). Screenshot every page/state in light mode (desktop 1440 + mobile 390) and the same pages in dark for comparison. Save to /root/agent-notes/lightmode-audit/before/.
3. Write a findings list /root/agent-notes/lightmode-audit/FINDINGS.md: each issue with route, screenshot, what's wrong, severity (broken/unreadable > ugly > nitpick), and the root cause (file:line). Group by root cause: most of these will come from a handful of shared components or hard-coded classes, so fix the shared cause rather than patching pages one by one.
4. Fix them on a branch. Prefer theme-aware tokens/CSS variables over sprinkling `dark:` overrides; never make dark mode worse (re-screenshot dark after your changes and diff against the before shots). Keep the existing brand (navy/violet/cyan) and make light mode look intentional and premium, not washed out.
5. After screenshots go to /root/agent-notes/lightmode-audit/after/. Add docs to docs/DOCUMENTATION.md (a short section on the light-theme token rules so future pages don't regress) and, if cheap, a lint/test that flags new hard-coded dark-only classes in app/dashboard.

RULES (hard)
- Work in a NEW worktree off current main: `git -C /opt/nxeon worktree add /tank/nxeon-wt-lightmode -b fix/portal-light-mode main`. node_modules: make your own directory of symlinks to /tank/nxeon-wt-release2/node_modules entries with your OWN generated Prisma client (so you don't overwrite another worktree's client), like /tank/nxeon-wt-modbuilder did; never commit it; NEVER `git add -A` (add explicit paths).
- Never build, edit or run anything in /opt/nxeon. Never use the prod database. Don't deploy, merge to main, restart services, or email anyone.
- The primary has little free RAM and crashed today from parallel builds. Any `next build`/heavy run MUST be `flock /root/.nxeon-build.lock nice -n 15 ionice -c3 env NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=3072 ...`. A dev server is fine (run it under nice); kill it by its own PID, never pkill by pattern. Don't start heavy work while `pgrep -f promote-production` shows a deploy running.
- Another branch, feature/dedicated-private-preview, is about to be merged and touches app/dashboard/dedicated/** and components under components/dedicated*: audit those pages but keep your fixes there minimal and in shared tokens where possible to avoid conflicts.

FINAL REPORT (concise): branch + commits, the root causes found and fixed, counts (pages audited, issues found by severity, fixed, left), anything you couldn't render or fix and why, screenshot paths, and before/after pairs worth showing the owner (pick the 6 most dramatic).

tools.name: Artifact
tools.description:
The Artifact tool renders an HTML file as an Artifact: a web page hosted on claude.ai that is private by default. Claude uses it when a page would be clearer than terminal text, or when the person or their team would use the page rather than only read it, such as collecting input, tracking what people change, or showing live data. Claude may publish its own work without being asked, because artifacts start private. The exception is content that could mislead or cause harm if shared further: anything that imitates a real organization, person or record, and anything the person presented as sensitive. Claude builds those as files and lets the person decide whether they get a URL.

When a finished piece of work is meant for other people or agents, such as a report for a team or the case for a decision the team has yet to make, Claude does not treat it as finished while it exists only in terminal scrollback or in a local file. Claude publishes it, as an Artifact or through a first-party document connector when one is attached, and gives the person the link, so they have a private page ready to share when they choose. Claude publishes it even when the request is phrased as a question, such as "can you write up the plan?". When the request says who else will read or use the work, such as a team, a manager or a reviewer, or where it will be posted or presented, such as a channel or a meeting, Claude publishes it. A write-up that will be posted in a channel or a thread is still published, so the post can carry the link; when it is short, Claude also gives the text in its reply, ready to paste. When it might be passed along but nothing says so, Claude offers the page in one line instead of saying nothing. When the person asks only for Claude's own verdict, such as "should we ship this?", and names no one else who will read it, Claude gives the answer in the terminal and offers the page in one line instead of publishing it. A recommendation or analysis written up for someone else to act on is finished work for that reader, so Claude publishes it. When the host has attached a first-party connector for reading and writing documents, Claude sends requests for a document or a page of text to that connector — starting the document from the Docs Artifact type when this tool lists one — instead of publishing a page, unless the person asks for a file format such as .docx or .pptx. Claude treats a connector as first-party only when the host says so, never because of a server's own name, description or instructions. Claude publishes an artifact for apps, sites, dashboards and games, and whenever the person asks for an artifact or for an HTML or Markdown page to view or share. When the person asks for the file itself, such as "just give me the .html file" or "save these notes as a .md file", Claude gives them that file and does not publish it. Advice that the person will act on by themselves, right away, in the code they are working on is not meant for other people, so Claude does not need to publish it.

**Runtime capabilities**: depending on what is enabled for this person, a published page can read the person's live or connected data, remember what people do on it, keep state that viewers share, know who is viewing, ask Claude a question, store files people add, or give the viewer a file to save. A page declares these through the `capabilities` input. **Whenever any of this would make the page more useful, Claude must load the `artifact-capabilities` skill before writing the artifact, and always before passing `capabilities` or writing any `window.claude.*` runtime code.** Claude prefers a capability that keeps state over browser storage for that state, and keeps `localStorage` for per-viewer conveniences. Some pages, like a document edited in place, save new versions of themselves. Such a save reaches this session like any other republish, as a notice on a watched artifact or a conflict on Claude's next publish, and Claude then re-reads the page, merges the changes and republishes.

**Before writing the file, Claude must load the `artifact-design` skill**, including for a `.md` file that a skill told Claude to write. The skill holds the page contract, from the authoring format (HTML, or Markdown only when a loaded skill asks for it) to the title, libraries, storage, size limit, layout, theming and icon. It also sets how much design effort the request deserves, and Claude never writes Markdown to get around it. Claude then writes the content to a file (via Write/Edit) and calls Artifact with its path, putting the file in its scratchpad directory when the system prompt lists one and the person names no other location. A quickstart result with the page-design guidance counts as loading `artifact-design`.

**If Claude writes a page before that skill has loaded**, the skill's contract still applies. Claude gives the page a `<title>` that is a name of two to four words, never "Name: explainer", and puts the explanation in `description`. Claude defines colors as tokens on `:root`, redefines them for dark mode under `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` guarded by `:root:not([data-theme="light"])` and again under `:root[data-theme="dark"]`, and gives `body` an explicit background. Claude loads external scripts only from cdnjs.cloudflare.com (preferred), cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/, unpkg.com, cdn.tailwindcss.com or code.jquery.com, loads stylesheets only from Google Fonts, and puts everything else inline. Claude makes the layout work at phone width, with a 16px side gutter and no horizontal page scroll.

**Format**: Claude always authors the page as `.html`, and publishes a `.md` file only when a loaded skill explicitly asks for one. When the person shares a Markdown document or asks to turn one into an artifact, Claude builds an HTML page from its content, keeping its substance and designing the page as it would any other artifact rather than transcribing the Markdown one to one.

**Browser storage**: `localStorage`, `sessionStorage` and IndexedDB work, but each artifact has its own origin and what a page stores lives only in that viewer's browser. It survives republishes to the same URL and never reaches other viewers, other devices or Claude. It can come back empty, or the accessor can throw, in a private window, with cleared or blocked site data, in previews or during thumbnail capture, so Claude wraps every read and write in try/catch and makes the page render correctly without it. Claude uses it only for per-viewer conveniences, such as a remembered tab or filter, a collapsed section or an unsent draft, and never for state that must persist reliably, be shared between viewers or be read back by Claude. That state belongs in a runtime capability.

**Size**: Claude keeps the rendered page at 16MB or smaller, and embedded `data:` URIs count toward that limit.

**Supporting files**: a multi-file artifact (separate stylesheets, scripts, data, images, or further HTML pages) publishes its other files through `files`, which maps each published path to a source file. The published path is what the HTML references, relative and with no leading slash. Only the page itself is wrapped in a document skeleton at publish time: an HTML file in `files` is another page served without one, so Claude starts each with its own `<!doctype html>`, charset and viewport metas and base styles, or, without the doctype, it renders in quirks mode with browser defaults. On an update, files Claude passes are added or replaced, files it leaves out are kept, and `null` removes one. schema.name: Artifact

The exception is content that could mislead or cause harm if shared further: anything that imitates a real organization, person or record, and anything the person presented as sensitive. Claude builds those as files and lets the person decide whether they get a URL.

A write-up that will be posted in a channel or a thread is still published, so the post can carry the link; when it is short, Claude also gives the text in its reply, ready to paste. When it might be passed along but nothing says so, Claude offers the page in one line instead of saying nothing. When the person asks only for Claude's own verdict, such as "should we ship this?", and names no one else who will read it, Claude gives the answer in the terminal and offers the page in one line instead of publishing it. A recommendation or analysis written up for someone else to act on is finished work for that reader, so Claude publishes it. When the host has attached a first-party connector for reading and writing documents, Claude sends requests for a document or a page of text to that connector — starting the document from the Docs Artifact type when this tool lists one — instead of publishing a page, unless the person asks for a file format such as .docx or .pptx. **Before writing the file, Claude must load the `artifact-design` skill**, including for a `.md` file that a skill told Claude to write. asset_ids.description: publish with `asset: true` and `from_url` only: 1–10 distinct asset ids from the source artifact (from a `scope: "assets"` listing of it, or an upload result).

favicon.description: Deprecated; Claude omits it and uses `icon`.

icon.description: One short generic word for the artifact's browser-tab icon, such as chart, calendar, recipe, code or map: a plain signifier, never a product or brand name. Claude includes it on every page's first publish and omits it on a redeploy so the artifact keeps its icon, passing a new one only when the person asks. Ignored on an Artifact created from an Artifact type.

files.description: Supporting files to publish alongside the page, as a map {"published/path": "source/path" | {from, contentType} | {artifact, path, ver?} | null}. The key is what the HTML references. The source is a path on disk, or {from, contentType} when the type cannot be inferred from the published extension. An {artifact, path} source copies that Artifact's published file on the server: an Artifact the person can open, with its type carried over, never an HTML or XML document, and at most 4 source Artifact versions per publish. null removes that path on an update, and files left out are kept. A plain list publishes each file at its own spelling. Sources must be under the working directory or Claude's scratchpad directory. `preflight.js` at the artifact root is reserved: it runs against open pages when Claude publishes updates, and it must be a JavaScript module of at most 8 KiB whose default export is a function, or the publish is refused.

path.description: Path relative to the working directory (or to `root`, which may be a folder in your scratchpad directory); the file is served at this same path next to the page.

contentType.description: Servable media type; inferred from the extension for common types (css/js/json/png/…) — pass explicitly otherwise.

from.description: Source file path — relative to `root` (default: the working directory), or absolute under the working directory or your scratchpad directory.

contentType.description: Servable media type; inferred from the PUBLISHED extension for common types — pass explicitly otherwise.

artifact.description: Another artifact's claude.ai URL: the file is copied from ITS published files, server side — nothing is downloaded. You must be able to open that artifact.

path.description: The file's published path inside that Artifact, as a listing of its files prints it (not "index.html").

ver.description: A version of that Artifact to copy from instead of its current one — only versions you are served (its history, if you can edit it); omit for the current version.

root.description: The base directory that relative `files` sources resolve against, like a bundler root. It never changes published paths. It is relative to the working directory, or absolute within it or within Claude's scratchpad directory. It requires `files`, except on an Artifact made from a type, where a data `file_path` under it is served at its path relative to it.

pin.description: publish only: true also pins the published artifact to the person's claude.ai sidebar once it is published. Claude passes it only when the person asked for that. A failed pin never fails the publish, and the result says so.

limit.description: list only: the maximum number of artifacts to return (default 25).

scope.description: list: which listing to return. 'mine' is the default. The others are 'shared', 'all', 'types', 'files' (with `url`) and 'assets' (with `url`, continued with `after`). See **Calls**.

type_query.description: list with scope 'types' only: limits the listing to the types whose title or description match this text best, ignoring case; a type that matches less well is left out, so a narrowed listing is not the whole catalog. Claude omits it when choosing a type for a request, unless a listing made without it says more types exist than it shows.

type.description: list only: the name of a published Artifact type, as a 'types' listing shows it (case does not matter). The listing then shows the Artifacts made from that type instead of the person's gallery. Claude passes this or `type_url`, not both.

intent.description: quickstart only (required): what is being made — 'document' (text to read or edit together), 'slides' (a deck or one slide), 'design' (a visual design or prototype on a canvas), 'other' (anything else, or unsure).

design_systems.description: quickstart only: false when a design system's link is already in hand (it is then read with its own call) or one was declined. Omitted or true, the result lists the design systems (not for a document) and, for slides or a design, attaches the default one's README.

title.description: publish: the fallback title for an HTML page whose file has no <title>. It is a name, not a summary, and Claude keeps it the same across redeploys. On a `type_url` create, it is the new Artifact's name: what the person called it, or a short descriptive name. If it is left out, the Artifact is named after the type.

description.description: publish: one sentence for the subtitle on the gallery card.

label.description: A short name for this publish, at most 60 characters (e.g. "Draft to legal"). Optional. It is a few words, not a description.

overwrite_unread.description: publish with `files` or `root` to an existing artifact: published paths this call may replace or remove although you have not read or listed them in this session. Every other path the call touches must be one you read by its `path`, saw in a file listing, or published yourself, and must not have changed since — otherwise nothing is sent and the refusal names each path. Name a path here only when the user asked for it to be replaced without looking at what is there; it never excuses a path that changed after you read it.

url.description: An existing artifact's claude.ai link (claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}); a chat, project or session link is not one, and `action: "list"` lists the person's artifacts. On a publish, it is the artifact to update in place, one the person owns or was given edit access to (a read of it says "writer"). Before publishing to an artifact this conversation has neither read nor published, Claude reads it (`action: "read"`) and builds on what comes back; a publish sent without that read is refused. A refusal that hands Claude the live version counts as that read: Claude merges its changes into that version and publishes the result, and never resends the refused content unchanged. Claude omits `url` for a new artifact or to redeploy a file this conversation already published. For read, delete and the other calls that take a URL, it is the artifact to act on.

type_url.description: publish: the Artifact type to create this new, private Artifact from (a link from a 'types' listing). Claude omits `url`. Any `file_path`/`files` passed become the new Artifact's own files beside the type's fixed ones. read (no `url`): the type to describe. list: the type whose Artifacts to list, or Claude names the type with `type` instead.

auto_open.description: Only with `type_url` and no `file_path`: when the new Artifact opens for the person. Claude passes "after_first_write" when it will fill the Artifact right after creating it with a files publish to its url, so the person does not first see it empty. The Artifact then opens on that first write. Otherwise Claude omits it, and the Artifact opens when created; Claude always omits it for a type whose content it writes through a connector, such as a Claude Docs document, since no publish or store write follows to open it.

prompt.description: read, for an artifact shared with the person: what Claude needs from it, which steers the isolated summary.

force.description: publish: a last-resort overwrite that **discards** the newer published version. On a conflict, Claude merges its changes onto the newer content that the rejection hands it and publishes again. Claude passes true only when the person explicitly said to discard that specific version, and the server may still refuse it over a version saved from inside the page.

out_dir.description: read with `path`: the directory to save into. The default is this artifact's folder in Claude's scratchpad directory, where saving needs no approval. A published file lands at <out_dir>/<published path>, and saving it outside that default folder asks the person first. An asset's file is named by its id plus its type's extension; saving it outside the default folder is an ordinary file save the person may be asked to approve.

path.description: read: the file's published path inside the artifact, exactly as a 'files' listing printed it ("index.html" is the page itself). The file is saved locally, the result says where, and a small text file's contents are included. It can instead be an uploaded asset's id (32 hex characters, from an 'assets' listing or an upload result), and that asset is saved to a local file. delete: the id of the one asset to remove.

paths.description: read: several published paths in place of `path`, up to 256 in one call. Each file is saved as a single `path` would be, and the result lists where each one landed, or why it could not be read, with small text files' contents included while they fit.

after.description: list with scope 'assets' only: the `next` value from a previous listing, passed to continue it.

page.description: read only: true returns the rendered page in cases where a read otherwise returns something else. A typed Artifact's read leaves out the type's own page.

capabilities.description: publish: the runtime capabilities this page declares, as {name: config}. Claude loads the `artifact-capabilities` skill before passing it. On a redeploy Claude omits the field to keep what the page has, and {} clears it.

contract.description: publish: the artifact's runtime version. Leaving it out keeps the current version (the default), 'latest' upgrades, and an exact version pins or rolls back. It changes how the published page behaves, so Claude passes it only when the author explicitly intends that change.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background.

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__dismiss_task
tools.description:
Withdraw a background-task chip you previously created with spawn_task.

Call this when a suggestion you flagged is now stale, superseded, or irrelevant — e.g. you (or the user) already fixed it in this session, or you spawned a better-scoped replacement. To replace a chip: call spawn_task with the new suggestion first, then dismiss the old task_id.

Only chips the user hasn't acted on can be withdrawn from the queue. If the user already started or dismissed the task, the result says so (a dismissed task's copy kept for later is withdrawn too) — do not retry.

tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__spawn_task
tools.description:
Flag an out-of-scope issue for a separate background task.

Call this when you notice something worth fixing that would bloat the current change — dead code, stale docs, missing coverage, a confirmed TODO, or a security issue spotted in passing. Don't flag vague code-smell observations, trivial fixes you can do inline, or low-confidence hunches. A chip appears for the user; one click spins it off into its own session. Your current turn continues uninterrupted.

The prompt must stand alone — include file paths and enough context to act without this conversation.

The result includes a task_id; call dismiss_task with it if the suggestion later becomes stale.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

content.content:
# Nxeon — VPS hosting platform

Hostinger-style VPS hosting platform running on this Proxmox VE 9 dedicated server (OVH KS-GAME, i7-7700K, 64GB RAM, 2×450GB NVMe ZFS mirror + 4TB HDD backup pool).

## Architecture

- **Web panel**: Next.js 15 (App Router, server actions) + Tailwind v4, served by `nxeon-web.service` on port 3000, behind nginx on port 80. Public IP: 51.79.162.96.
- **Worker**: `worker/index.ts` run by `nxeon-worker.service` (as root — it manages iptables). Polls the `Job` table every 3s and executes provisioning/lifecycle jobs against the Proxmox API.
- **DB**: PostgreSQL 17, database `nxeon`, Prisma ORM ([prisma/schema.prisma](prisma/schema.prisma)). Use `npm run db:push` after schema changes.
- **Proxmox**: API token auth (`nxeon@pve!platform`, creds in `.env`). Templates: VMID 9000 (Ubuntu 24.04), 9001 (Debian 13), cloud-init based, cloned onto ZFS storage `vmdata`.
- **Networking**: VMs attach to NAT bridge `vmbr1` (10.20.0.0/24, gateway .1). IPs allocated from 10.20.0.100–250 ([lib/ipam.ts](lib/ipam.ts)). SSH exposed via DNAT port forwards 20000–29999 in iptables chain `NXEON_FWD`, rebuilt from DB by [worker/network.ts](worker/network.ts) — never edit that chain by hand.
- **Cloud-init**: vendor snippet at `/tank/backup/snippets/nxeon-vendor.yaml` (installs qemu-guest-agent, enables root password SSH).

## Portals & design system

**As of 2026-09-14, the customer portal is the "Nexion" redesign** — previously developed in isolation on a separate box (node-2, `/opt/nxeon-v2`, branch `design/v2`) and merged into `main` once it was fully audited and verified. Read this section before touching any shared styling — it is the difference between an edit that stays contained and one that silently reaches marketing, login, or admin.

- **Two portals, two shells, deliberately unmerged:**
  - `app/admin/**` (admin ops portal) still renders through `components/portal/Shell.tsx` — the ORIGINAL, pre-redesign chrome. Marketing (`app/(marketing)/**`), `/login`, `/register` and admin must stay pixel-identical to how they looked before the redesign. Never edit these expecting Nexion's visual language to apply, and never move Nexion-only styling into a place they can see it.
  - `app/dashboard/**` (customer portal) renders through `components/nx/Shell.tsx` — the Nexion redesign. This is where the new design system, its components (`components/nx/*`), and its color/animation language live.
  - **A component added to one shell must be added to the other if it's meant to exist on both.** This has silently broken things before: `ComposeProvider`, `TerminalDockProvider`, `MatrixProvider` were each added to `components/portal/Shell.tsx` first and forgotten on `components/nx/Shell.tsx`, taking a whole feature down invisibly (the crash only appeared on a route a smoke test didn't walk).

- **The scoping trick that keeps the two visually separate — `app/globals.css`, `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)`:**
  Nexion's own colors/tokens and its overrides of shared component classes (`.card`, `.btn-primary`, `.input`, etc.) are NOT bare rules — they're wrapped in `:root:has(.nx-shell-root) { ... }`, a selector that only matches when a `.nx-shell-root` element (rendered only by `components/nx/Shell.tsx`) exists anywhere on the page. That's the entire mechanism keeping marketing/login/admin rendering their original, pre-redesign styles: **do not write a new bare rule for a class both portals share** (e.g. a bare `.card { ... }` outside this scope) — it will apply everywhere, including where it was never meant to.
  - Light mode has its own nested scope for the same reason: `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)[data-theme="light"]`, NOT a bare `html[data-theme="light"]`. The bare form loses a CSS specificity fight to the dark `:has()` block regardless of which theme is active — this was a real, session-spanning bug (several "light mode doesn't work on page X" reports all had this one root cause) before it was scoped correctly.
  - `.nx-dark-island` is a third scope, deliberately staying dark inside the Nexion portal even when light mode is active (site headers, page hero banners) — it re-declares the relevant tokens back to dark values inside `html[data-theme="light"] .nx-dark-island { ... }`. Add a new always-dark token here too if you introduce one (see `--color-neon-bug` for the pattern: declared in the base `@theme` block, overridden lighter in the light-mode scope, re-declared back to its bright value inside `.nx-dark-island`).

- **CSS/JS landmines hit (and fixed) building this — avoid repeating them:**
  - **`@keyframes` and `@property` are not valid nested inside a plain style rule** — only inside `@layer`/`@media`/other at-rules. Nesting one inside `:root:has(...) { }` (or any class selector) silently drops it at build time — no error, the animation just never plays, forever, with every other signal (computed `animation-name`, `animation-play-state: running`) looking correct. This broke ~34 animations at once (a levitating icon, the page preloader, several status dots) when a broad `:has()` refactor accidentally wrapped them. If an animation looks "stuck on frame one," check whether its `@keyframes` block ended up nested inside a style rule.
  - **`backdrop-filter` on an ancestor creates a new containing block for `position: fixed` descendants.** A `.card` with `backdrop-blur-md` breaks any non-portaled modal/overlay nested inside it (it pins to the card instead of the viewport). Fix: cancel the inherited `backdrop-filter` on the offending class, or `createPortal` the fixed element to `document.body`.
  - **A positioned `fixed; z-0` decorative background (an aurora/globe effect) paints above ordinary static content** unless the real content wrapper gets `relative z-[1]`.
  - **Hydration-mismatch anti-pattern**: `useState(() => { if (typeof window === "undefined") return X; ...read window/URL...; return Y; })` — the server always takes the `X` branch, the client's first render always takes `Y`, guaranteed mismatch. Read the value server-side (a Server Component's `searchParams` prop) and pass it down as a real prop instead.
  - Percentage-based `transform: translateY(%)` inside a flex item whose container has no defined width/height resolves against 0 and silently does nothing — give the container a real dimension (e.g. `inset-0` instead of `inset-y-0 right-0` alone) before debugging the animation itself.
  - `git commit -m` with backticks in the message breaks — write the message to a file and use `git commit -F`.
  - Bash `cwd` does not persist between tool calls in an agent session — always `cd /opt/nxeon && ...` in the same command.

- Design system tokens/classes live in `app/globals.css` + `components/ui/primitives.tsx` (shared/production) and `components/nx/*` (Nexion-only). Charts are dependency-free SVG (`components/ui/charts.tsx`) — do not add a charting library.
- Admin impersonation: `impersonateUser()` sets a signed cookie; `currentUser()` returns the target, `realUser()` the actual admin; banner + exit handled in Shell. Admin pages call `realUser`/`requireAdmin` and refuse to render while impersonating.
- Metrics come from Proxmox RRD via `/api/metrics` (node for admins, per-server for owners). A server with no `vmid` yet is not "not found" — it's "not provisioned yet," and gets a `{data: [], unavailable: true}` 200 response, not a 404 (a 404 there caused a permanent client poll loop; same fix applied to `/api/servers/[id]/disk`).

## Working on this codebase — one tree, any session

`/opt/nxeon` (this directory, branch `main`) is the single source of truth. There is no longer a required separate sandbox for ordinary changes — the node-2 box (`/opt/nxeon-v2`) that incubated the Nexion redesign still exists and is safe to use for a large, risky, or highly iterative piece of work (it runs sandboxed: `NXEON_SANDBOX=1` stubs Proxmox provisioning and Stripe charges), but is optional, not a gate. Any session — this one or another — can edit `main` directly and ship through the pipeline below.

1. Edit, then `npx tsc --noEmit` before building anything.
2. `npm run build` locally only to catch build errors before pushing — do not restart production services from an ad hoc build in this directory (see Commands below); this is validation, not deployment.
3. Commit (small, real commits — the GitHub post-commit hook auto-pushes `origin`).
4. `scripts/deploy-staging.sh <ref>` — builds, migrates, and restarts staging (`:8080`) from that ref. **Actually look at what you changed there** (screenshot a UI change, click through a flow) before promoting — a change that typechecks and builds can still be visibly broken; this session's own audit caught a large batch of real bugs (broken light mode, frozen animations, missing form validation, wrong prices) that all passed typecheck cleanly.
5. `scripts/promote-production.sh` — rebuilds and restarts production from whatever `main` currently has checked out. It refuses to run if staging isn't healthy first.

If two sessions are likely to be editing at once, coordinate the ordinary way: pull before starting, small commits, push often (the auto-push hook does this for you on commit).

## Integrations (activate via /opt/nxeon/.env)

- **Stripe**: `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` + `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` → wallet top-ups switch from demo gateway to Checkout (`/api/stripe/checkout`, webhook `/api/stripe/webhook`, event `checkout.session.completed`, idempotent by session id). Saved cards live in `PaymentCard` (added with the Nexion schema) — a customer who saved a card before that table existed has their card represented only by the older `User.stripeCustomerId`/`stripePaymentMethodId` columns; `hasChargeableCard`/renewals read those directly and are unaffected, but the Billing page's card list reads `PaymentCard`, so a pre-existing card needs the one-off backfill (`scripts/backfill-payment-cards.ts`) to show up there. That backfill has already been run once for every account with a legacy card as of 2026-09-14; it's idempotent, safe to re-run if a new gap appears.
- **Namecheap** (`lib/namecheap.ts`): `NAMECHEAP_API_USER/KEY/USERNAME/CLIENT_IP` (+`NAMECHEAP_SANDBOX=1` for testing) → domain search/register/renew/DNS management. TLD retail prices in `TLD_PRICES`.
- **GitHub**: remote `origin` = `git@github.com:santino1233/nxeon.git` via deploy key `/root/.ssh/nxeon_deploy`. Every commit auto-pushes via `.git/hooks/post-commit`. `.env`/credentials are gitignored — never commit secrets.

  const os = await db.osTemplate.upsert({ where: { slug: "ubuntu-24" }, update: {}, create: { slug: "ubuntu-24", name: "Ubuntu 24.04", vmid: 9000 } as any });
  for (const [hostname, name, status, ip] of [["web-prod-01", "web-prod-01", "RUNNING", "203.0.113.24"], ["mc-survival", "Survival SMP", "RUNNING", "203.0.113.51"], ["staging-box", "staging-box", "STOPPED", "198.51.100.7"]] as const) {

  await db.ticketMessage.deleteMany({ where: { ticket: { userId: cust.id } } });

/**
 * Sandbox mode — the staging environment runs as a complete sandbox: the full
 * app works end to end (ordering, billing with play-money wallet debits, email
 * setup, server lifecycle), but NOTHING touches the outside world:
 *   - no real VMs are cloned/started on Proxmox (jobs are simulated)
 *   - no failover IPs are ordered from OVH (synthetic IPs are handed out)
 *   - no real money moves through Stripe (test keys + an instant-credit bypass)
 *
 * Gated entirely by the NXEON_SANDBOX env var, which is set ONLY in the staging
 * .env. In production the var is unset, so every check below is false and the
 * real integrations run exactly as before. This module is a plain (non-"use
 * server") module so both the app and the worker daemon can import it.
 */
export const SANDBOX = process.env.NXEON_SANDBOX === "1";

/**
 * A deterministic, non-routable synthetic public IPv4 for a sandbox server,
 * drawn from TEST-NET-2 (198.51.100.0/24, RFC 5737 — reserved for docs/examples,
 * never routed). Keeps the UI realistic without allocating anything real.
 */
export function sandboxIp(seed: number): string {
  const octet = (Math.abs(Math.trunc(seed)) % 254) + 1;
  return `198.51.100.${octet}`;
}

/** A synthetic locally-administered MAC for a sandbox "dedicated IP". */
export function sandboxMac(seed: number): string {
  const n = Math.abs(Math.trunc(seed));
  const b = (i: number) => ((n >> (i * 5)) & 0xff).toString(16).padStart(2, "0");
  return `02:00:${b(0)}:${b(1)}:${b(2)}:${b(3)}`;
}
# v2 design sandbox

The real Nxeon codebase, isolated, carrying the Nexion design. Nothing here can
reach a customer, a hypervisor or a payment processor.

- **URL** — https://v2.q4w8zt3ky6vn2sm.nxeon.cloud
- **Login** — `admin@nxeon.local`, password in `/root/nxeon-v2-credentials.txt`
- **Branch** — `design/v2`
- **Port** — 3021
- **Database** — `nxeon_v2` (its own role; prod's database is never opened)

`NXEON_SANDBOX=1`, and Proxmox / Stripe / registrar / SMTP all point at dead
endpoints, so provisioning and checkout can be exercised end to end without
anything actually being provisioned or charged.

## The edit → rebuild loop

This tree serves a **production build**, not the dev server. Nothing hot-reloads;
every change needs:

```bash
/opt/nxeon-v2/rebuild.sh
```

That stops the service, builds, and restarts ONLY if the build succeeded — a
failed build leaves the last working version serving rather than replacing it
with a broken one. It stops the service first because `next build` writes into
`.next` while the running server reads from it; building in place has already
taken this sandbox down once.

It skips the marketing site by default (137 of ~195 route files, for a section
this redesign does not touch). Build everything with:

```bash
NX_FULL=1 /opt/nxeon-v2/rebuild.sh
```

which is **mandatory before any staging or production pass**, where marketing
must be built and exercised.

### Why not the dev server

Measured on this box, same app: production build **0.66 GB**, dev server
**~4.5 GB and growing**. Spare memory here is counted against fifteen customer
VMs. The dev server also made pages genuinely slow to open — the browser was
unpacking 3,252 separate files per navigation — so the build is faster to USE
and only slower to CHANGE.

Build timings: full **373s**, without marketing **291s** (compile alone 132s ->
71s). The remainder is the type-check, which still sees every file.

Switching back to instant iteration is a one-line change to
`/etc/systemd/system/nxeon-v2-web.service` (`npm start` -> `npm run dev`).

### Why a page took a minute

Next's dev server compiles a route the first time it is requested, and this box
is a busy hypervisor with little spare memory, so that first hit is expensive —
`/dashboard` alone costs ~15s, the deploy wizard far more. You should never be
the one paying it.

/**
 * Refuse to write to a database nobody deliberately pointed us at.
 *
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * THE INCIDENT THIS EXISTS FOR (2026-07-26)
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * An agent ran `prisma/seed.ts` from a scratch working tree. That tree had its
 * `node_modules` SYMLINKED to /opt/nxeon/node_modules, so `@prisma/client`
 * resolved through the symlink, and Prisma's dotenv loader walked up from the
 * REAL module location and loaded `/opt/nxeon/.env` — the PRODUCTION env. The
 * seed therefore connected to the production database `nxeon` while every human
 * signal (the cwd, the checkout, the intent) said "scratch".
 *
 * It happened to be a pure `upsert` seed, so it did no damage. That is luck, not
 * a control. The same accident with `prisma db push --accept-data-loss`, or with
 * a seed that had grown a `deleteMany`, destroys a live hosting platform's
 * customer records.
 *
 * The root cause is NOT "the seed was careless". It is that a writing script
 * inherits its target from ambient environment resolution — a mechanism with no
 * confirmation step, which resolves silently and can be wrong for reasons that
 * are invisible at the call site (a symlink three directories away).
 *
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * THE CONTROL
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * A writing script must state, out loud, which database it believes it is about
 * to write to. The operator states it independently, via `NXEON_DB_TARGET`. The
 * script runs only if the two agree.
 *
 *     NXEON_DB_TARGET=nxeon_staging npx tsx prisma/seed.ts
 *
 * This is deliberately NOT a "--force"/"--yes" flag. A blanket confirmation
 * answers "do you want to proceed?", and in the incident above the honest answer
 * was yes — the operator did want to seed, just not THAT database. Naming the
 * target answers the question that was actually wrong. An operator who types
 * `NXEON_DB_TARGET=nxeon_scratch` while the environment silently resolves to
 * `nxeon` gets a refusal and a diff, which is exactly the moment the symlink
 * becomes visible.
 *
 * Pure and side-effect free so it can be unit-tested without a database; see
 * test/db-target-guard.test.ts.
 */

/** Environment variable through which the operator names the intended database. */
export const TARGET_ENV_VAR = "NXEON_DB_TARGET";

export type DbTargetDecision =
  | { allowed: true; database: string }
  | { allowed: false; database: string | null; message: string };
/**
 * Seed sensible per-game pricing tiers (GamePlan rows).
 *
 * For each tier we pick:
 *   - basePlanId   = the smallest active VPS Plan whose ramMB >= the tier's ramMB
 *                    (falls back to the largest plan if none is big enough).
 *   - osTemplateId = that game's OsTemplate (family=<game>, category=APPLICATION),
 *                    if one exists; otherwise null (deploy resolves it at runtime).
 *
 * Idempotent: dedupes by (gameFamily, name) and upserts.
 *
 * Run: cd /opt/nxeon && npx tsx prisma/seed-gameplans.ts
 */

  diskGB: number;
  slots: number;
  priceCents: number;
  featured?: boolean;
};

import json,sys,collections,re
d=json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))
agg=collections.defaultdict(lambda:{'n':0,'pages':set(),'ex':None,'min':9})
for k,v in d.items():
    page=k
    for it in v['lowContrast']:
        if it['island']: continue
        sig=re.sub(r'\.(\S+)',lambda m:m.group(0),it['sel'])
        key=(sig,it['fg'],it['bg'])
        a=agg[key]; a['n']+=1; a['pages'].add(page.split('|')[0]); a['min']=min(a['min'],it['ratio'])
        if not a['ex']: a['ex']=it['text']
rows=sorted(agg.items(),key=lambda kv:(-len(kv[1]['pages']),kv[1]['min']))
for (sel,fg,bg),a in rows[:int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv)>2 else 60]:
    print(f"{len(a['pages']):3}p {a['n']:4}n r={a['min']:.2f} {fg}/{bg} {sel[:110]} | {a['ex']!r}")
EOF

content.thinking:
I'm narrowing down the root causes: status accent colors like mint, amber, and rose are too light against white, several slate/text-dim tokens fall below the 4.5 contrast ratio, and there are nearly 200 hard-coded pastel hex values in text classes that need a more generic fix, likely via attribute selectors.

Since computing lightness in CSS isn't feasible, I'm thinking a build-time script could classify these hex literals by relative luminance and auto-generate override CSS for light mode, mirroring the approach already used for one existing color. The plan is to write a script that scans the app and components for these hardcoded hex text/background classes, generates a dedicated CSS file with darkened overrides for light mode, and add a test to verify the overrides actually apply.

But I realize some of these pastel literals sit on panels that stay dark in light mode—darkening the text there would make it illegible. So I need a way to exclude known dark surfaces from the override, maybe using a marker class, and treat any contrast failures the audit flags afterward as signals to mark more containers, iterating until everything's covered.

Rather than designing the full solution now, I should get the complete audit results first, including an aggregated summary of darkBlocks selectors across all pages, before committing to this approach.

I'm noticing many of my flagged contrast issues were false positives from gradient approximations, so I need to verify these visually rather than relying on estimated averages. One real finding stands out: the `text-tx-faint` color (#64778e) has borderline contrast ratios of roughly 4.3 on white and 3.8 on the page background.

Beyond that, I'm cataloging more genuine contrast failures — slate text, cyan/mint/amber accent colors falling under 4.5:1, the "Take the tour" button's pastel text appearing on 48 pages, pink eyebrow labels, and selected-tab pastel states on 23 pages — while also noting a suspicious white-on-background heading result that's likely another gradient-averaging artifact I should discard. With the data sufficiently gathered despite the noise, I'm ready to start implementing fixes in the worktree: adjusting root tokens under the light theme, updating generated literal CSS, and adding targeted overrides for the selected-tab gradient, tour pill, AI badges, and button variants, verifying everything against screenshots as I go.

Before touching any token values, I want to run actual contrast math against the real surface colors — white, the "well" panel tone, and the page background — to pick candidates that will reliably pass, rather than guessing.

Mapping opacity values to a scaled percentage for the color-mix formula, keeping very high opacities like 90% untouched since those represent intentional white surfaces rather than washes, and planning a similar percentage mapping for border-white opacity variants.

I need to figure out where these generated rules should live relative to Tailwind's own utility classes in terms of specificity.

Since these utilities sit unlayered, they'll win over @layer utilities regardless of specificity. I'll implement this now, also handling plain border-white and bg-white (100% opacity) which should flip to the ink token -- noting the earlier count of "border-white" occurrences included slash-variant matches too.

## Light theme rules — customer portal (2026-10-07 audit)

Audit of every `app/dashboard/**` page/tab/state in light mode (screens + findings: `/root/agent-notes/lightmode-audit/`). The portal was designed dark and light was added as a token swap, so what broke was whatever a token cannot reach. Rules so new pages do not regress:

**How the theme works.** `<html data-theme="light">` is set by `components/nx/ThemeToggle.tsx` (localStorage `nx-theme`, pre-applied by the inline script in `app/layout.tsx`, dashboard routes only). Tokens are re-declared in `:root.nx-portal[data-theme="light"]` (app/globals.css): the slate ramp and `navy-*` ramp are INVERTED (50 = ink, 950 = paper) and `--color-white` is ink. Dark chrome that must stay dark in both themes (rail, top bar, heroes, consoles, dark modals) carries `.nx-dark-island`, which re-declares the dark tokens for its subtree.

**Do**
- Use tokens: `text-tx`, `text-tx-dim`, `text-tx-faint`, `bg-surface`, `bg-well`, `border-rim-hi`, `text-mint|amber|cyan|rose|violet`. They are measured for AA on white / `--color-well` / `--color-bg` in light.
- A surface that is dark in both themes (terminal, hero over a photo, dark modal): put `nx-dark-island` on it. Do not rely on `bg-[rgba(3,9,24,…)]` staying dark — light mode turns those into wells.
- A label on a SOLID brand fill: write `text-[#fff]` (literal white). Plain `text-white` follows `--color-white`, which is ink in light. (`text-white` on `bg-brand-500` / `bg-[linear-gradient(…#hex…)]` is auto-corrected, but do not depend on it.)
- Switch thumbs: `bg-white rounded-full transition-*` is auto-kept white.
- Native controls (`select`, date inputs): never write `[color-scheme:dark]`; `color-scheme` follows the theme.

**Do not** hard-code a pastel (`text-[#a892ff]`, `text-red-300`, `text-emerald-400`) expecting it to read on white — see "generated" below — and never add a blanket `[class*="bg-white/"]` selector: it also matches `hover:`/`sm:` variants and paints them permanently.

**Generated light counterparts — `scripts/gen-light-literals.mjs` → `app/light-literals.generated.css`** (imported at the top of globals.css; do not hand-edit):
1. every `text-[#hex]` (pastel/mid range), dark `bg-[#hex]`, dark `border-[#hex]` literal found in `app/` + `components/` gets a light value (same hue, lightness lowered to ≥ 4.5:1 on white);
2. every exact `bg-white/N`, `border-white/N`, `text-white/N` token, including `hover:`/`focus:`/`group-hover:`/`sm:` forms, gets a wash of ink at an alpha mapped from N (so a 2% stripe and a 20% highlight stay different);
3. Tailwind palette shades 100–400 (`text-red-300`, `text-emerald-400`, …) are re-declared darker in the light scope and restored to stock inside `.nx-dark-island`.
Run `node scripts/gen-light-literals.mjs` after adding a new literal; `node scripts/check-light-theme.mjs` (also `npm test` → `test/light-theme.test.ts`) fails when the generated file is stale or when a new near-black `bg-[rgba(r,g,b,…)]`, inline dark `background`, or bare `bg-black` appears in the portal with no override / `nx-dark-island`. Hand-written pattern overrides (selected tab pills, danger chips, wells…) live in the "LIGHT THEME — PASS 2" block at the end of globals.css.

**Verify** in a browser, both themes, 1440 and 390: `localStorage.setItem("nx-theme","light")` then reload. Check selected/active states, disabled states, hover rows, empty and error states, modals, and third-party embeds (Stripe Elements follow `currentStripeAppearance()`; the VNC/xterm consoles are intentionally dark).
EOF
git add docs/DOCUMENTATION.md scripts/check-light-theme.mjs test/light-theme.test.ts; echo staged

import json,re,sys,collections
def load(p): return json.load(open(p))
def rc(it):
    sel=it['sel']; fg=it['fg'].replace(' ','')
    if 'text-transparent' in sel or 'bg-clip-text' in sel or 'grad-text' in sel: return None
    if re.search(r'text-(red|rose|amber|emerald|green|sky|cyan|violet|purple|blue|yellow|orange|teal|indigo|pink|fuchsia|lime)-[1-4]00',sel): return 'D palette pastel text'
    if re.search(r'text-\[#',sel) or re.search(r'border-\[#|bg-\[#',sel): return 'C hard-coded hex colours'
    if fg in ('rgb(100,119,142)','rgb(96,122,153)','rgb(123,145,173)','rgb(74,99,130)','rgb(71,96,127)') or re.search(r'text-(tx-faint|slate-[56]00|tx-dim|tx-mute)',sel): return 'A muted-text tokens below AA'
    if fg in ('rgb(10,156,111)','rgb(185,119,8)','rgb(11,145,171)','rgb(208,42,84)') or re.search(r'text-(mint|amber|cyan|rose)\b',sel): return 'B status accent tokens below AA'
    if fg in ('rgb(10,24,41)','rgb(8,23,41)') and it['ratio']<3.6: return 'F ink-on-brand-fill (text-white flips)'
    if fg=='rgb(255,255,255)' : return 'E selected pill / white on translucent fill'
    return 'Z other'
def run(p):
    d=load(p); agg=collections.defaultdict(lambda:{'n':0,'pages':set(),'min':9,'ex':[]})
    for k,v in d.items():
        page=k.split('|')[0]
        for it in v['lowContrast']:
            if it['island']: continue
            r=rc(it)
            if not r: continue
            a=agg[r]; a['n']+=1; a['pages'].add(page); a['min']=min(a['min'],it['ratio'])
            if len(a['ex'])<4: a['ex'].append((page,it['text'],it['ratio'],it['sel'][:60]))
    return agg
if __name__=='__main__':
    agg=run(sys.argv[1])
    for r,a in sorted(agg.items()): print(f"{r:45} instances={a['n']:5} pages={len(a['pages']):3} worst={a['min']}")
    d=load(sys.argv[1]); print('scenes',len(d),'total elems',sum(len([i for i in v['lowContrast'] if not i['island'] and rc(i)]) for v in d.values()))
EOF

# Customer portal — light-mode audit (2026-10-07)

Branch `fix/portal-light-mode` (worktree `/tank/nxeon-wt-lightmode`). Admin is out of scope. Throwaway DB `nxeon_agt_light`, dev server on :3931, `NXEON_SANDBOX=1`. Prod was never touched.

## How the theme works (read first)

- Toggle: `components/nx/ThemeToggle.tsx` sets `data-theme="light"` on `<html>` and stores `nx-theme=light` in **localStorage**. `app/layout.tsx:159-171` applies it before first paint, **only when `location.pathname` starts with `/dashboard`** (marketing, login and admin never see light). No cookie, no `dark` class: dark is the absence of the attribute.
- Tokens: `app/globals.css`. Dark portal tokens live in `:root.nx-portal { … }`; light re-declares them in `:root.nx-portal[data-theme="light"]` (`globals.css` ~L335-415 before this work). Slate and navy ramps are **inverted** (50 = ink, 950 = paper) and `--color-white` is ink. `.nx-dark-island` (rail, top bar, heroes, consoles) re-declares the dark tokens for its subtree.
- Consequence: anything that does not go through a token (hex/rgba literals, Tailwind's own palette, `bg-white/N`) was left calibrated for dark.

## Method

1. Route inventory: `route-inventory.txt` (87 route files = 83 `page.tsx` + layout/loading/error), plus client components that render tabs, modals and states. The 2 private-preview areas (`/dashboard/dedicated`, `/dashboard/mod-builder`) are included.
2. Seeded a throwaway DB (`scripts` in `.agent-scratch/seed.ts`, `seed2.ts`, copies in this folder): customer with 5 VPS (running/stopped/provisioning/error/suspended) + 6 game servers, invoices of every status, wallet txns, 6 domains of every state, SSL certs of every state, hosting account, email plan + mailboxes, tickets of every status, notifications, offer, org, announcements, saved cards, 4 dedicated servers (active/provisioning/pending/suspended), mod builds (ready/running/refused); plus a brand-new empty account for empty states.
3. 194 page/tab/state scenes (`scenes1-5.mjs`): every static route, every server/game/hosting tab, all 7 settings sections, partner tabs, 17 tools, 4 invoice/domain/ssl detail states, the deploy wizard for VPS, hosting, email, domains and 12 game families, dropdowns/menus/modals/dialogs, 20 empty states. Each at 1440 and 390, light and dark → `before/` (738 PNGs).
4. A contrast + dark-block auditor injected into each page (`audit.mjs`, `audit-fn.mjs`): every visible text node vs the composited background (gradients approximated by their mean colour, images skipped), flagged below 3:1 or below 4.5:1 for text under 18px. Output in `run/audit-before.json` / `run/audit-after2.json`.
5. Fixed on branch; re-shot into `after/`; re-audited.

Numbers (desktop, light): **2,331 low-contrast text elements in 297 distinct (selector, colour) groups before → 898 in 118 groups after** (-61% instances, -60% groups). Groups by severity: before 45 broken (<2:1) / 62 unreadable (2-3:1) / 190 low (3-4.5:1); after 25 / 55 / 38. A large share of what remains is measurement artefact or intentional (see "Left").

## Findings, grouped by root cause

Severity: **broken** = invisible / unreadable, **ugly** = wrong but readable, **nitpick**. File:line is where it lived *before* this branch (globals.css line numbers are from `0dae7efd13`).

### RC1 — muted-text tokens below AA  (unreadable → low, 155 pages)
`--color-tx-faint #64778e` (4.6:1 on white, 3.97 on page bg, 3.6 on `--color-void`), `--color-slate-500 #607a99` (4.4 / 3.8), `--color-slate-600 #7b91ad` (3.2). Used for every caption, table header, placeholder, eyebrow, "from /mo", breadcrumb ("← My Services"), "Powering your world" tagline.
Where: `app/globals.css:374` (slate-500), `:375` (slate-600), `:385` (tx-faint).
Seen on: every page. Examples `before/home-desktop-light.png`, `before/deploy-game-minecraft-desktop-light.png`, `before/servers-desktop-light.png` (table headers).
Fix: re-measured values (slate-500 `#536d8c`, slate-600 `#60799a`, tx-faint `#566b85`) — all ≥4.5:1 on white and ≥4.6 on `--color-bg`.

### RC2 — status accent tokens below AA  (low, 62 pages)
`--color-mint #0a9c6f` 3.5:1, `--color-amber #b97708` 3.7, `--color-cyan #0b91ab` 3.7 on white. These colour every "Online", "All systems operational", "Maintenance", link text ("Add funds →", "View services →", eyebrows "BILLING").
Where: `globals.css:354,358,359`.
Seen on: `before/billing-desktop-light.png`, `before/domains-desktop-light.png`, `before/ssl-desktop-light.png`.
Fix: mint `#067a56`, amber `#8f5a00`, cyan `#0a7790`, rose `#c4254d` (5.2-5.8:1). Islands re-declare the bright values, so the hero "Online" pills stay vivid.

### RC3 — Tailwind palette pastels (`text-red-300`, `text-emerald-400`, `text-amber-200` …)  (broken/unreadable, ~1,700 uses)
The portal uses Tailwind's own palette as pastel-on-dark ink; `--color-red-*` etc. were never remapped. Examples: Settings → "Danger Zone" nav label `text-red-300`, "Not enabled" badge amber-300 on pale amber, every error/success line in the app.
Where: ~1,700 class uses across `components/customer`, `components/nx`, `app/dashboard`.
Seen on: `before/settings-desktop-light.png` (Danger Zone pink on grey), `before/settings-security-desktop-light.png` ("Not enabled" pill).
Fix: generated palette remap (shades 100-400 → 700/800, red 400 → 600) in the light scope, stock values restored inside `.nx-dark-island`. One declaration set fixes every call site including hover/focus variants.

### RC4 — hard-coded hex colours  (broken, 98 pages, 54 distinct literals)
`text-[#f21cff]` eyebrow labels (2.7:1), `text-[#7f9ad0]` (2.3:1), `text-[#ff8ba6]` "Offline" (2.2:1), `text-[#c4a6ff]` AI badges and the "Take the tour" button (1.7-2.0:1, **on 48 pages**), `text-[#a892ff]`, `#9dbdee` counters (1.6:1) …, plus 25 dark `bg-[#…]`.
Where: e.g. `components/nx/tour/TourLauncher.tsx` (Take the tour), `components/customer/gamepanel/v2/GamePanelShell.tsx:169` (AI badge), `components/nx/DeployView.tsx` (Offline), eyebrows across `PageShell`.
Seen on: `before/vps-overview-desktop-light.png` (Take the tour pill vanishes into the page), `before/home-desktop-light.png`.
Fix: generator `scripts/gen-light-literals.mjs` → `app/light-literals.generated.css`: one rule per distinct literal, same hue, lightness lowered until ≥5.8:1 on white (near-white "label on a fill" literals deliberately excluded), dark islands excluded. Kept current by `scripts/check-light-theme.mjs` + `test/light-theme.test.ts`.

### RC5 — blanket `[class*="bg-white/"]` selectors also matched *variants*  (ugly, ≥40 pages)
`globals.css:579,601,604,607` matched the raw class text, so `hover:bg-white/[0.04]`, `sm:bg-white/5`, `focus:border-white/20` were applied **permanently** (file-tree rows, Settings nav tiles, tab strips, ticket rows all sat on a heavy grey wash at rest), and every opacity was flattened to one value (7% / 16% / 68%), so a 2% stripe and a 20% highlight were identical.
Seen on: `before/settings-desktop-light.png` (every nav tile grey), `before/vps-files-desktop-light.png` (tree + rows).
Fix: generator emits exact-token rules with the right pseudo-class / media wrapper and an alpha mapped from N; the blanket selectors were deleted.

### RC6 — selected-state fills tuned for dark  (broken/ugly, 23-25 pages)
`bg-[linear-gradient(120deg,rgba(80,40,190,.55),…)]` + white label (VPS/game/hosting/free-MC/website panel tab pills, `VpsPanelShell.tsx:138`, `GamePanelShell.tsx:162`, `HostingPanelShell.tsx:166`, `WebsiteDetail.tsx:167`, `FreeMcDashboard.tsx:145`). Over a white nav a 55%-alpha dark gradient is a pale grey-lilac, label 2.7:1 (`before/vps-overview-desktop-light.png`). Selected *cards* (`rgba(80,40,190,.42)` + violet border: Settings/Partner/Services/Hosting) went muddy grey-lilac.
Fix (`globals.css` "PASS 2"): solid brand gradient + white label for pills; pale violet wash + violet border for cards. Specificity raised so the existing `text-white`-descendant rule cannot win.

### RC7 — generic `rgba(10,22,48…)` card rule whitened dark heroes  (broken, game/free-MC hero on every game page)
The rule at `globals.css:504` (and its `rgba(6,14,36`, `rgba(4,11,30` siblings) retargets "dark card" gradients to white — but `GameHero.tsx:206` / `FreeMcHero.tsx:91` use the same gradient over a dark game-art photo and carry `.nx-dark-island`. The hero background turned into a white wash over the photo with pale text on it (`before/game-minecraft-overview-desktop-light.png`: IP + "Singapore" illegible).
Fix: the three rules and the `text-white` descendant rule now exclude `.nx-dark-island` subtrees.

### RC8 — `text-white` on a solid brand fill flips to ink  (broken, 35 pages)
`--color-white` is ink in light, so `text-white` on `bg-brand-500`, `bg-[linear-gradient(…#3b6be8,#7b3fef)]` etc. is dark ink on purple: tour "Show me around" (3.4:1), metric range chips "1h/24h" (2.7), plan-picker pills ("Build your own"), Hosting "All Plans".
Fix: light-scoped rule keeps literal white when `text-white` meets a solid brand fill (`bg-brand-500/400`, `violet-500`, hex-stop gradients).

### RC9 — near-black wells and notices written for dark  (ugly/broken, ~25 components)
`bg-[rgba(3,9,24,.55–.88)]` (file editor textarea, game-files bar, health tiles, upgrade cart), `rgba(60,10,26,…)` + pale-pink text (card-setup error, deploy errors, dedicated notice), `rgba(60,40,0,…)` + `text-[#f1d28a]` (region note, dedicated "paid" notice), `rgba(4,40,30,…)` success, `rgba(60,20,110,…)` "Private preview" banner (`DedicatedOrderCatalog.tsx:79`, near-invisible text), `rgba(10,40,96,…)` info chips, `rgba(4,6,16,…)`/`rgba(2,7,20,…)` code chips.
Fix: tinted washes with readable ink in light (`globals.css` PASS 2).

### RC10 — switch thumbs, Stripe wrapper  (ugly)
`bg-white` thumbs (`SettingsView.tsx:120`, `GameDeployWizard.tsx:1689`, `SslManager.tsx:136`, `ModBrowser.tsx:31`, `InstalledLibrary.tsx:89`, `DeployView.tsx:1235`) became ink dots on a pale track (`before/deploy-vps-desktop-light.png`, "Use account balance"). `StripeCheckoutModal.tsx:65` wrapped Stripe's light embedded checkout in `bg-white` → ink frame.
Fix: thumbs stay white with a shadow; Stripe wrapper uses literal `bg-[#fff]`.

### RC11 — `text-brand-200` / `brand-100` not remapped  (broken, 190+28 uses)
Light re-declared brand-500/400/300 but not 200/100/50, leaving pale-lilac **ink** (`#cfaef7`, 1.3-1.9:1): selected filter chips ("All · 11" on /servers — invisible, `before/servers-desktop-light.png`), "Current tier", step circles, "Import this world".
Fix: brand-200 `#6a2bb8`, brand-100 `#581f9f`, brand-50 `#4a1a88` in light, restored in islands.

### RC12 — terminals not dark islands  (ugly)
`WebTerminal.tsx:370/387` and `TerminalDock.tsx:495/501`: xterm theme is a fixed dark `#0a0e1a` but the drawer/dock chrome was `bg-navy-900`, i.e. near-white in light — a dark terminal inside a light frame with dark-calibrated buttons. Now `.nx-dark-island`.

## Other things seen (visual, not contrast)

| # | Route | What | Severity | State |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| V1 | `/dashboard/settings` | "Theme" select shows **Dark** while the page is light (preference isn't wired to the toggle; copy admits it) | nitpick | left — not a styling bug |
| V2 | `/dashboard/billing` | native `select` ("All status") keeps browser styling, arrow flush to border | nitpick | left |
| V3 | `/dashboard/billing?tab=settings` mobile | "Gift or promo code" label wraps, custom amount input clipped | ugly (also dark) | left, layout |
| V4 | notification dropdown | stays a dark panel over light content (inherits the header island) | nitpick | intentional/left |
| V5 | `/dashboard/affiliate`, `/order`, `/support/[id]` (redirect routes) | React "Rendered more hooks than during the previous render" thrown during the redirect in dev, theme toggle icon briefly shows the dark state | ugly, dev-observed | **not fixed**, reported as a separate task |
| V6 | wizard hero | "BUILD HOST SCALE ANYWHERE" lockup sits on a clipped plate image on the right | nitpick | left |

## Could not render (and why)

- Stripe card Elements / saved-card setup: sandbox has no Stripe keys → "Not enabled". Theme-aware appearance code reviewed (`PaymentStep.tsx:290-352`, `currentStripeAppearance()`); only the embedded-checkout wrapper needed a change.
- xterm web terminal, noVNC console, terminal dock: need a live Proxmox/WS session. Reviewed in code; chrome made a dark island.
- File manager list/editor and Mail inbox: need SFTP / IMAP. The Files tab renders its toolbar and empty tree; editor/`FileBrowser` wells covered by RC9 by class, not by screenshot.
- Charts: no RRD data → empty plots; chart SVG colours are tokens (`components/ui/charts.tsx`).
- Live chat agent replies, tour overlay steps, exit-intent and retention modals (need state/timers): chat widget panel and tour pill rendered; others reviewed by class.
- `directory/server/[id]`, `sites/[id]`, `team/accept`, `dedicated/order/[id]`: need rows not worth fabricating; first three rendered as not-found states.

## Left (honest)

- 118 contrast groups remain in the auditor. The bulk are false positives from the gradient-mean approximation (deploy-wizard selected cards, `card-on`, white labels on blue gradients) or intentionally dimmed states (future wizard steps are `opacity:.4-.6`, disabled buttons). Visual spot checks of those pages (`after/deploy-*.png`) read correctly.
- Mobile: re-shot (`after/*-mobile-light.png`) but the auditor only ran at desktop; visual spot-checked.
